tracks.title: Total Prizes Available
tracks.description: Prizes will be awarded amongst all submissions. Top submissions will be highlighted at a Google hosted expo during NeurIPS 2026. Prizes awarded for this competition are the following:

prizes.title: Overall Best Paper - $15,000
prizes.description: Overall best paper will be award the highest score calculated as the average of all five criteria.

prizes.title: Best New Resource (Dataset, library, etc) - $10,000
prizes.description: A resource introduces a new dataset, tool, or software, for example. This is compared to an empirical paper which generates new knowledge/experiments. For examples of each, a new ‘dataset’ could leverage the provided embeddings or other sources to create a dataset that can be used for either evaluation of Gemma 4 or for fine-tuning it. A new ‘tool’ could be a library which uses Gemma and some other algorithm to cluster code based on underlying behavior. New ‘software’ could be a dashboard to explore Github repos that are similar in structure to a target repo.

prizes.title: Best New Application - $10,000
prizes.description: A novel application is a new use-case (e.g. using code-graphs for writing TPU kernels). Show your creative uses of code-graphs and/or the provided embeddings to create novel use-cases. This may involve creating new evaluation datasets for entirely novel tasks. It could also involve application to existing benchmarks that differ from the provided ones, and using the code-graphs or embeddings where they have not been used before.
